composition.serve_who: GMMS 108′-111 is the vessel’s +24 V DC distribution schedule. Its named AFT-panel, FWD-panel, Emergency Power Supply and Emergency Panel breaker banks serve the individual loads named on each row, while the left service-supply one-line serves the main bilge pump, fire pump and tender winch. The bus bars, CT-monitored incomers, panel-to-panel feeders and terminal strip T/S E are distribution infrastructure owned by the DC-distribution system, not by the downstream equipment.

infrastructure.system_name: 24 V Service Supply and high-current branch section
facts: The left vertical conductor is titled 24V SERVICE SUPPLY and feeds parallel fused branches.
F7/SW8/SO6 feeds the main bilge pump; F8/SW9/SO7 feeds the electric fire pump; an F? 50A/SW? branch feeds the tender winch.
F5 100A via SW6 and F6 200A via SW7 continue to destinations not identified on this sheet.
CT8 surrounds a drawn feeder continuing to ONYX and is identified in the notes as QI-POWER-485-LV.
Diamond numbers 70, 95 and 35 are conductor-size callouts, not devices.
A separately titled AFT PANEL DC BREAKERS section contains Q1–Q54 on drawn panel bus bars.
Q33, Q34, Q53 and Q54 are spare/unused rows marked '/'.
The upper auxiliary breaker bank Q45–Q54 is fed from the AFT panel bus; Q47 reaches a drawn relay contact before B&G.
CT9 and CT10 are current monitors on the watermaker and autopilot-pump branches respectively.
A separately titled FWD PANEL DC BREAKERS section contains normal breakers Q1–Q20 and emergency breakers QE1–QE4.
The long upper supply conductor is drawn into the FWD panel normal bus.
The emergency feeder from Emergency Power Supply QE6 is drawn to the FWD emergency section via continuation marker 6.
QE2–QE4 are spare/unused rows marked '/'.
The separately titled EMERGENCY POWER SUPPLY receives the +24 V emergency-battery feeder through CT7, with upstream continuation to drawing 111a and a separate continuation to ONYX.
Its bus feeds QE1–QE8; QE1 32A feeds the separate Emergency Panel, and QE6 20A feeds the FWD panel emergency section.
QE5 is a spare/unused 20A row marked '/'.
CT7 is identified in the notes as QI-POWER-485-300-LV.
The separately titled EMERGENCY PANEL is fed only by the drawn QE1 32A EMERGENCY SUPPLY path from the Emergency Power Supply.
Its bus feeds CB5 10A NAV. LIGHTS, CB6 15A EMERGENCY LTS, CB7 6A GMDSS, and CB8 6A CHART TABLE LT.
The CB6 emergency-light output is drawn through T/S E terminal 5 and continuation marker 4; terminals 6 and 7 are shown but have no drawn branch connection on this sheet.

uncertainties: The upstream source identity for the 24 V SERVICE SUPPLY bus and the +24 V emergency-battery feeder is off-sheet; only the drawn continuations are known.
F5 100A/SW6 and F6 200A/SW7 have no named destination on this sheet, so they cannot be attached to downstream equipment.
The tender-winch fuse and switch identifiers are printed F? and SW?; their 50A fuse rating and function are clear.
The relay identifier on the B&G path is only legible as Re?; its contact is drawn in series after Q47, but its coil command source is not established on this sheet.

CB7 6A is labelled GMDSS, but the register contains a GMDSS battery-bank node rather than a fitting GMDSS communications-load node; it is therefore retained as Emergency Panel infrastructure and not forced onto the battery node.
The 'AUX 1' portion of Emergency Power Supply QE8 has no fitting equipment node; only the B&G association is attached.
All downstream return conductors and most load-side controls are omitted from this distribution schedule; scenarios stop at the named load rather than inventing returns or command loops.
No fused-terminal symbol is present in the drawn T/S E path; terminals 5–7 are ordinary terminal points as drawn, so no built-in replaceable fuse is inferred.
